All of the federal agencies engaged in wide-scale programs involving land would be affected. We object to the features of this bill, which would mandate federal land and water resources agencies to protect species which are not truly endangered, but which might at some time in the future become endangered. This we feel gives an extremely wide discretionary authority to the Secretary of the Interior with no effective checks and balances and could, if abused, place unreasonable restrictions on justifiable federal and land and water resource programs.
Department of Natural Resources - Executive Office
The Department is opposed to the legislation that is currently under consideration. The Department feels that the individual States are in the best position to determine endangered species and that the responsibility for this should continue to rest with the State. The individual states are in a better position to determine if individual species are endangered in any one particular state. Where a species is endangered, the individual state can enact meaningful controls to protect the species endangered.
If the Secretary of the Interior is given discretionary authority in the designation of species which may sometime in the future become endangered, the action of placing these species on the endangered species, could limit or place unreasonable restrictions on justifiable federal and state land and water resource programs. For these reasons, the Department of Natural Resources is opposed to the proposed legislation.
